content_md:
So here's my opinionated product approach. Eager to hear pushback.

In groups as small as N=2, if any participant is sufficiently incentivized to leak a secret, they will leak. Leaks happen in low-stakes situations and leaks happen in [high-stakes situations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_government_group_chat_leaks).

Encryption-at-rest is a solved technical problem. But it does not really provide security for multi-person communications.

At best, it makes it hard for a person to sit at your unlocked computer and double-click on a file.

With messaging apps, it doesn't solve for a significant other grabbing a phone and/or gently requesting it to be unlocked.

At worst, it lets you unintentionally lose access to something you didn't intend to burn, via an opaque and unfamiliar process.
